questions.Q1: Demand: who buys off-the-shelf photo and video, in what unit and volume, and why instead of custom?
questions.Q2: Build, list, or both: what does listing on someone else's marketplace get a provider that building its own does not?
questions.Q3: Supply and rights: where does inventory come from (own collection, commissioned work, third parties, contributors) and on what rights is each listed?
questions.Q4: Channel conflict: how are resale rights carved out of commissioned work, and what happened when terms were changed after the fact?
questions.Q5: Operator's legal role: reseller, agent or venue; who is licensor of record, who warrants consent, who indemnifies?
questions.Q6: Custody: platform-hosted, shared in place from the provider's storage, or copied into the buyer's storage?
questions.Q7: Consent for onward sale, by party: the capturer, the person depicted, the place or property owner.
questions.Q8: Licence terms and defensibility once the file has left: exclusivity, audit, leakage, fingerprinting.
questions.Q9: How deals close: self-serve checkout or contact-sales; commission, revenue share, or owning the inventory.
questions.Q10: Object model: what a listing, dataset, revision, order and entitlement are; what a past buyer gets on a new version or a withdrawal.
questions.Q11: Samples, trust and quality evidence: what is shown before purchase, and which evidence buyers rely on.
questions.Q12: Catalogue and custom together: how the off-the-shelf side and the bespoke side relate, and what each is called.

matrix_definitions.operator_role: Who the buyer contracts with for the licence. reseller_licensor: the platform itself is licensor of record. agent: the platform sells on the provider's behalf under the provider's name. venue: the platform only hosts the listing and the provider is seller and licensor.
matrix_definitions.economics_model: How the operator earns from a dataset sale. commission: a percentage fee on the provider's sale. revenue_share: the contributor or provider receives a share and the operator keeps the rest (stock-media style). principal_margin: the operator owns or buys the data and sells at its own price.
matrix_definitions.who_pays_fee: Who bears the operator's fee: the buyer on top of the price, the seller out of proceeds, or both.
matrix_definitions.supply_models: Every source of listed inventory the evidence shows. commissioned_nonexclusive: data first collected for a paying client and then also sold to others. client_relisting: a buyer lists data it bought or owns.
matrix_definitions.custody_model: Where the bytes sit when a buyer gets access. share_in_place: read access to the provider's own storage, no copy. copy_to_buyer: data copied or delivered into the buyer's storage. links_only: the platform distributes URLs or metadata and the media stays on third-party hosts.
matrix_definitions.transaction_mode: How a purchase actually completes. contact_sales: price and licence settled with a salesperson; a 'request a quote' button counts.
matrix_definitions.public_prices: Prices published anywhere by the platform itself, including press releases and pricing pages. some: some listings or tiers have a published price.
matrix_definitions.licence_model: standard_licence: one licence for everything. tiered_standard: a fixed menu (for example research vs commercial). provider_defined: each provider sets its own licence. negotiated: settled per deal.
matrix_definitions.exclusivity_offered: Whether a buyer can obtain exclusive rights to a listed dataset, at any price.
matrix_definitions.public_listing: What an anonymous visitor can see.
matrix_definitions.buyer_vetting: What the platform checks about a buyer before a sale.
matrix_definitions.sample_mechanics: What a buyer can inspect before paying.
matrix_definitions.versioning: immutable_revisions: a published version never changes and a buyer keeps access to the versions bought. withdrawn_and_replaced: the dataset was pulled and reissued under a new name.
matrix_definitions.human_subject_consent_docs: For data showing people: whether the buyer receives consent or release evidence, gets only a warranty that it exists, or nothing.
matrix_definitions.contributor_pay_model: How the INDIVIDUALS who captured or created the content are paid when it is sold: crowd workers, photographers, uploaders. Not organisations supplying whole datasets; that is economics_model.
matrix_definitions.erasure_after_sale: What happens to copies already sold when content must come out (a data subject's request, a takedown). contractual_deletion: buyers are obliged by contract to delete, including on licence termination. takedown_only: the platform removes the listing but buyers keep their copies.
matrix_definitions.catalogue_plus_custom: Whether the organisation sells ready-made datasets, collects to order, or both.
matrix_definitions.quality_evidence: Whether quality statements on a listing were checked by the operator or are the provider's own.
